faq.q: Which is cheaper: Marbella or Estepona boat rental?
faq.a: Direct boat rental prices from our Puerto Banús fleet start at €749/2h (Astondoa 40, Azimut 39). Estepona operators tend to have smaller fleets and fewer luxury yachts, so pricing can be similar or slightly lower for comparable boats. faq.q: Can I rent a boat in Marbella and sail to Estepona?
faq.a: Absolutely. From Puerto Banús, it's about 12 nautical miles south to Estepona – a 30–40 minute cruise at 20 knots. Many of our boats, like the Azimut 58 Flybridge or Mangusta 80, easily cover this distance. You can anchor off Estepona's Playa de la Rada or visit the marina for lunch.

faq.q: What size boats are available in Marbella vs Estepona?
faq.a: Our Marbella fleet ranges from 6.4m (Mariah SX21) to 29m (Ferretti 94) with capacities from 5 to 12 passengers. Estepona marinas typically host smaller private boats (8–12m) and fewer luxury charters. For large groups or superyacht experiences, Puerto Banús is the better choice.

Estepona offers quieter coves like Cala del Faro and Cala Cortés, with calm waters and fewer crowds. Marbella has vibrant spots like Cabopino and the coastline near Río Verde, but they can be busier in peak season. If you want seclusion, choose Estepona; for social vibes, Marbella.

faq.q: What is the best time of year for boat rental in Marbella vs Estepona?
faq.a: Both destinations are excellent from May to October, with sea temperatures averaging 22–26°C. July and August are peak months with higher demand and prices. For a quieter experience, June or September offer great weather and fewer boats on the water.

faq.q: Do I need a license to rent a boat in Marbella or Estepona?
faq.a: No, because all our charters include a licensed skipper. This applies to both Marbella and Estepona rentals. You can relax and enjoy the coast without worrying about navigation. For self-drive options, a valid boating license is required, but we do not offer bareboat charters.

data.body_html:
Planning a boat rental on the Costa del Sol for 2032? The choice often comes down to two iconic destinations: Marbella and Estepona. Both offer stunning Mediterranean coastlines, but they cater to different tastes. Marbella, centred on the glamorous Puerto Banús, boasts a fleet of 19 luxury yachts from €749/2h, while Estepona provides a quieter, more authentic Andalusian experience. This guide compares marbella vs estepona boat rental 2032 across key factors – price, fleet, anchorages, and vibe – so you can book with confidence.

Fleet Size and Boat Options

Our Marbella fleet, departing from Puerto Banús, includes 19 vessels ranging from the compact 6.4m Mariah SX21 (5 pax) to the superyacht Ferretti 94 (29m, 12 pax). Estepona’s marinas (Puerto Deportivo and Puerto Estepona) host smaller charter fleets, typically with boats under 15m. For variety and luxury, Marbella wins – you can choose a speedboat for €749/2h or a 24m Mangusta 80 with a jet ski included from €4,719/4h. Estepona is better for intimate, budget-friendly trips.

Pricing Comparison

Our Tier A boats (Astondoa 40, Azimut 39) cost €749 for 2 hours or €2,299 for a full day (8h), including skipper, fuel, drinks, snacks, insurance, and VAT. Tier B (Mangusta 80 white/grey) starts at €4,719 for a minimum 4-hour charter, with a complimentary jet ski. Estepona operators often charge similar hourly rates but may exclude fuel or VAT. For transparent, all-inclusive pricing, Marbella offers better value.

Departure Points and Logistics

All our boats depart from Puerto Banús, Marbella – a 5-minute walk from the Golden Mile and 40 minutes from Málaga Airport. Estepona is 20–30 minutes south by car (AP-7) and has two marinas with ample parking. If you’re staying in Marbella, renting locally saves travel time. For those based in Estepona, a short drive to Puerto Banús opens up a larger fleet.

Anchorages and Scenery

From Puerto Banús, you can reach Cabopino (15 min), Cala del Faro (20 min), or Cala Cortés (25 min). Estepona offers quiet coves like Playa de la Rada and the coastline near Sotogrande. Marbella’s anchorages are busier but more social; Estepona’s are serene. For a mix, sail south from Marbella to Estepona in 30–40 minutes – our Azimut 58 Flybridge (17.6m, 12 pax) is ideal for this.

Onboard Experience and Inclusions

Every charter includes a licensed skipper, fuel, water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava, light snacks, insurance, safety equipment, and Spanish IVA (21%). No hidden costs. Our larger yachts (e.g., Ferretti 94, K80) feature flybridges, sundecks, and cabins. Estepona charters may offer similar amenities but often charge extra for premium drinks or jet skis. With us, what you see is what you pay.

Local Attractions and Vibe

Marbella is synonymous with luxury – think Puerto Banús superyachts, designer boutiques, and beach clubs like Ocean Club. Estepona is more traditional: whitewashed old town, tapas bars, and a relaxed promenade. For a party charter, choose Marbella. For a cultural day out with family, Estepona shines. Both are within easy reach of each other, so you can combine them on a longer charter.

Booking Tips for 2032

Book early for July and August – our fleet is popular. Use WhatsApp for pricing on boats not listed in Tier A or B (most are price on request). Consider a half-day charter (4h) to explore both Marbella and Estepona. Check our main page for the full fleet and availability. For the best of both worlds, rent from Marbella and sail to Estepona for lunch – it’s a 12 NM trip that showcases the Costa del Sol at its finest.
